stem:
A 66-year-old man begins a medication that blocks beta-adrenergic receptors, slowing his heart rate.

Which of the following correctly characterizes the receptors bound by norepinephrine and epinephrine at sympathetic targets?

options.label: A
options.text: Alpha and beta classes, both of which are G protein-coupled receptors
options.misconception: None; both adrenergic classes signal through G proteins.
options.explanation: Norepinephrine and epinephrine share the alpha- and beta-adrenergic receptors, and unlike the cholinergic nicotinic channel, every adrenergic receptor is a G protein-coupled receptor acting through second messengers.

options.label: B
options.text: Alpha and beta classes, both of which are ligand-gated cation channels
options.misconception: The nicotinic receptor's structure is being attributed to adrenergic receptors.
options.explanation: Ligand-gated channels describe the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor; all alpha- and beta-adrenergic receptors are G protein-coupled, hence slower second-messenger effects.

options.label: C
options.text: Nicotinic and muscarinic classes with no cross-reactivity between them
options.misconception: The cholinergic classification is being applied to catecholamines.
options.explanation: Nicotinic and muscarinic receptors bind acetylcholine; adrenergic targets express alpha and beta receptors, which are G protein-coupled.

options.label: D
options.text: Intracellular receptors that migrate to the nucleus when bound
options.misconception: Steroid-hormone signaling is being attributed to catecholamines.
options.explanation: Epinephrine and norepinephrine are ligands for surface G protein-coupled receptors and never enter the cell to bind nuclear receptors; that pattern fits lipophilic steroid hormones.

options.label: E
options.text: Enzyme-linked receptors that phosphorylate their own cytoplasmic tails
options.misconception: Receptor-kinase signaling is being attributed to catecholamines.
options.explanation: Adrenergic receptors are not catalytic; they activate separate G proteins, which move to effector enzymes that generate second messengers such as cAMP.

context: Learning objective: classify adrenergic receptors. Norepinephrine and epinephrine bind alpha and beta receptors; all adrenergic receptors are G protein-coupled, in contrast to the ionotropic nicotinic receptor.
imageCaption: Sympathetic thoracolumbar vs parasympathetic craniosacral; adrenergic receptor subtypes.
